findings.message: Pass-state is locally verified rather than gate-attested, and all three edits are genuinely exercised. Locally: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean and `npx tsx --test 'src/**/__tests__/*.test.ts'` at 615 tests / 611 pass / 0 fail / 4 skipped. Two INDEPENDENT mutation checks were run so neither assertion rides on the other: restoring the 90% assistant cap fails with 'assistant bubble spans the full row', and restoring only border-left:2px solid var(--magenta) while leaving the width at 100% fails with 'the assistant bubble has no left rail'. The result was also rendered in headless Chrome against the real stylesheet and inspected — both rows now align on both edges with no rail. The daemon validate gate returned passed:false solely because its sandbox blocks every executing command; it confirmed the contract by inspection (scopeRespected:true) and independently caught a real defect in this Story — see the quality finding.

Graph grounding is hollow as usual for this module: both changed entries are whole-file diff entities with testsReaching: [] and no caller/callee edges, because the CSS under review lives inside the template string renderShell emits rather than in indexed symbols. Treating those empty edges as a coverage gap would manufacture a finding against the very file that contains the new assertions. Coverage was judged by execution, by the two mutation checks above, and by visual inspection of the render.

The test title contradicted its own assertions in the first cut of this change: it still read 'the assistant bubble spans ~90% (bumped from 88%); user bubble (82%) + wrapper (100%) unchanged' while the body asserted 100%/100% and no rail. The daemon validate gate caught it ('the rewritten test's title still claims 90%/82% while asserting 100%/100%') and it was corrected before commit. Worth recording rather than silently fixing, because a stale title is exactly how a suite drifts into lying about what it covers — the same failure mode, in a different place, as the vacuous assertions this and the preceding two Stories were filed against.

`.insrc-msg--user{align-items:flex-end}` is now visually inert: the user bubble fills the row, so there is no free space for the flex-end alignment to act on. It still correctly right-aligns the 'you' role label above the bubble, so it is NOT dead code and removing it would change the header alignment. Left in place deliberately and noted here so a later reader does not mistake it for leftover, or delete it expecting no visual effect.
